newsitem.title: USA: Rubin reiterates support for strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Rubin reiterates support for strong dollar.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Monday reiterated his support for a strong dollar, saying that would keep inflation and interest rates down.
"We believe a strong dollar is in our economic interests," Rubin told reporters before a speech to the International Development Conference. "That has been our policy and continues to be our policy."
He said he saw no signs of inflation reigniting and said the United States was on track for solid economic growth with low inflation.

News on Friday that non-farm payrolls jumped sharply last month fanned fears in financial markets that inflation was about to pick up but Rubin played down those fears although he added that policymakers always have to be watchful about inflation risks.
"I do not see signs of reigniting inflation," Rubin said.

The U.S. Treasury secretary declined comment on the recent steep fall in the Japanese stock market. But as he has done before he stressed the importance of domestic demand-led economic growth in Japan.
"Japan has an enormous self-interest in continuing to grow and we are very interested in their policies ... to continue that growth," Rubin said.
Rubin said he did not know whether the drop in the Japanese stock market would undercut the country's economic growth.
"It is very important that they continue to have domestic-led growth in Japan," he said.
The drop in the Tokyo stock market has raised fears about the health of Japanese banks.
In response to a question, Rubin said the United States was not taking any extraordinary action to monitor Japanese banking operations here in the United States.
He said that the Japanese government itself some time ago realized the need to focus on the banking system in Japan.
